gaps.sentence: We reached ___ agreement after hours of negotiation.
gaps.explanation: 'Reach an agreement' — 'agreement' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: ___ noise woke me up in the middle of the night.
gaps.explanation: 'The noise' — the one that woke me; 'in the night' is a fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: He behaves as if he were ___ owner of the company.
gaps.explanation: 'The owner' — there is one owner, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: She gets up at six and watches ___ morning news.
gaps.explanation: 'The morning news' — a specific known broadcast, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: He had ___ operation on his knee last year.
gaps.explanation: 'Operation' starts with a vowel sound, so 'an operation'.

gaps.sentence: She works as ___ waitress during the summer holidays.
gaps.explanation: After 'as' and 'work as', jobs take a/an: work as a waitress.

gaps.sentence: ___ Hyde Park is lovely in autumn.
gaps.explanation: Most park names take no article: Hyde Park, Central Park (exception: the Grands Boulevards style names).
Plural general nouns and flu (illness name) take no article.
